sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (true/false, match the columns, fill in the blanks or give reasons).

questions.q: Complete the table by selecting the appropriate fabric for each end use and giving one reason. Choose from cotton, nylon, wool, silk. End uses: summer clothing; winter sweater.
questions.answer: Summer clothing: cotton, because it absorbs perspiration and conducts heat away. Winter sweater: wool, because it is a bad conductor of heat and keeps the body warm.

questions.q: State whether True or False and correct the false one. (a) Synthetic fibres are ideal for baby's undergarments. (b) Doctors wear white coats to look fashionable.
questions.answer: (a) False: synthetics are non-absorbent; cotton is ideal. (b) False: white looks clean and protects against infection.

questions.q: Match Column I with Column II. I: (1) Baby garments (2) Teenagers (3) School-going children. II: (a) Variety to mix and match (b) Strong and durable (c) Absorbent cotton.
Fill in the blanks. (a) A ________ label gives characteristics such as size and variety. (b) The ________ Act, 1988 covers malpractices in selling textiles.
Justify. (a) A closely woven fabric is more serviceable. (b) Long floats in a weave should be avoided.
questions.answer: (a) It has more yarns so it is stronger. (b) Long floats snag easily and weaken the fabric.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What will you check in seams and fasteners while purchasing ready-made garments?
questions.answer: Check that seams are double, finished, free of puckers and have enough allowance. Open and close fasteners and zips to see that they work well.

questions.q: What is the difference between a label and a marking?
questions.answer: A label is a piece of paper, plastic or tag attached to a garment with information. A marking is printed on the surface of fabric or 'thaan' for identification.

questions.q: What three points would you check to ensure buying good quality fabric?
questions.answer: Check that the cloth is pleasing to touch and closely and evenly woven. Check for even dyeing with no powdery dust and a clean smell.

questions.q: Which three characteristics would you consider while buying clothes for summers?
questions.answer: The fabric should be absorbent like cotton. It should be light, loose and light-coloured and easy to launder.

or.q: Which three characteristics would you consider while buying clothes for your college-going sister?
or.answer: Fit and style that she likes, a mix-and-match combination for variety, and easy care and colour fastness.

questions.q: Why is cotton preferred for summer wear?
questions.answer: Cotton absorbs perspiration and is a good conductor of heat. It keeps the body cool.

questions.q: List any two malpractices in selling fabrics.
questions.answer: Giving less quantity by stretching the fabric or using a short rod. Selling seconds as fresh goods or giving misleading labels.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain the importance of labels and markings on textile products. How do they help consumers make informed decisions?
questions.answer: (i) Labels and markings give information on fibre content, brand, size and care. (ii) Care labels tell washing and ironing instructions and certification labels show standards such as the Woolmark. (iii) This helps consumers judge quality, avoid misleading goods and choose suitable clothes.

questions.q: What are the different malpractices prevalent in selling fabrics?
questions.answer: (i) Giving lesser quantity or poor quality by stretching the fabric. (ii) Cheating on price by charging more than the printed price. (iii) Selling defective goods as fresh and giving false or incomplete labels.

questions.q: How will you judge the quality of a fabric? (three points)
questions.answer: (i) Material and weave: pleasing to touch, closely and uniformly woven, no long floats. (ii) Finish: even dyeing, clean smell and no powder when rubbed. (iii) Check that yarns meet the selvedge at right angles and patterns are matched.

questions.q: Explain how care and maintenance and price affect the choice of ready-made garments (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Read the care label before buying. (ii) Choose fabric that needs minimum care and has fast colour. (iii) Price should match the quality and wear, since a high price is not always high quality.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Discuss the factors that influence the selection of clothing for different age groups, with examples for each age group.
questions.answer: (i) Infants need soft, light, absorbent cotton clothes with simple openings. (ii) School-going children need strong, durable, easy-to-launder clothes with extra seam allowance. (iii) Teenagers want fit and style and mix-and-match clothes for variety, such as a few salwars with several kameez or jeans with T-shirts. (iv) Adults, especially working women, need easy-care, wrinkle-free clothes. (v) Old people need light, loose clothes with front openings and large buttons. (vi) Climate, occasion and profession also influence selection.
